steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Food poisoning is illness caused by eating food contaminated with harmful bacteria, viruses, or toxins.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The main food poisoning bacteria include: Salmonella, E. coli (especially O157), Campylobacter, Staphylococcus aureus, and Clostridium perfringens.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Salmonella is commonly found in raw poultry and eggs; symptoms include diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal cramps.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: E. coli O157 is found in undercooked minced beef and unpasteurised milk; it can cause severe kidney damage (haemolytic uraemic syndrome).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the most common bacterial cause of food poisoning in the UK. | Q: What is the difference between food poisoning by infection and by intoxication? | Q: Which bacterium produces toxins in food and is carried on human skin?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Campylobacter, often found in undercooked poultry. | Infection: caused by eating food containing live bacteria that multiply in the gut. Intoxication: caused by eating food containing toxins already produced by bacteria before the food is eaten. | Staphylococcus aureus. It is carried on skin and in nasal passages, and can transfer to food through poor hand hygiene.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the specific sources, symptoms, and prevention methods for each key bacterium — examiners often ask you to name a bacterium linked to a specific food. Always distinguish between infection and intoxication when explaining how food poisoning occurs. When discussing prevention, use the '4 Cs': Cross-contamination, Cleaning, Chilling, and Cooking. Use precise names: 'Campylobacter' not 'campylobacter bacteria', 'E. coli O157' not just 'E. coli'.
